ambiguities.reading: The stat sample (p. 13) splits into exactly 80 items — no trailing '|' — and the field-count check (p. 11) counts the stat record, so stat carries none. The debt and alas samples each END with '|' (22 items for 21 fields, 9 for 8); the court counts neither, so they follow their samples.
The spec names no line ending. LF, one record per line, the last line terminated; CR never appears, so a parser that splits on LF alone reads no stray CR into a field.
No character set is named. Printable ASCII only (0x20-0x7E), never the delimiter; the builder folds accents to ASCII and refuses a value it cannot, rather than sending bytes the court may mis-decode.
The permitted range reaches -999999999999.99 (16 characters) but the Field Length is 15. The width wins: a value longer than 15 characters is refused.
'In decimal notation to two places' (field 25); the sample also shows '34442342.2' and '100'. Exactly two decimals, always.
'**' means each court decides (p. 11). Treated as required for an individual debtor, except the two blanks the spec itself allows: SSN when field 5 is not i, Tax ID/EIN when field 5 is i.

Release 5.1 accepts up to five comma-delimited values (pp. 11-12), but field 8 is 11 wide — exactly one SSN — and field 9 is 15 — one EIN. One value per field; a debtor with more cannot land and the builder says so.

The 'akatype' table is the court's, not reproduced. Only aka and fka (the sample's) are allowed; a business name the debtor used is sent as aka. dba is the likelier code for those — confirm a court's table on its training database (ADR 0024 PR 10) before adding it.

The record has one address. The mailing address when the debtor gave one (where the court's notices go), else the residence; the county (field 17) is always the residence county, which is the venue fact.

Field 72 must be a valid case number in the current court and needs the related case's office code (73), which the case record does not hold. Both are left blank; the related case stays on B101 line 10.

B122A-2 line 40's middle outcome (between the thresholds, go on to Part 4) has no code of its own; it is sent as u, and field 71 then carries line 42's answer. Below the median, or exempt, 122A-2 is not filed and 48-71 are blank.
These name Form 122A-1/122A-1Supp/122A-2 lines only (field 32 alone names 122C-1). A Chapter 13 case leaves 41-71 blank rather than putting 122C figures under 122A labels.
Ignored for Chapter 7 (set to n) and for 11/12/13 (set to y), but still required on a voluntary case: the builder sends what B101 line 17 answers on Chapter 7 and y otherwise.
Reserved for future use, so blank, although the stat sample puts y there.
